objective: Explain what friction does and give examples where it helps and where it hinders.
success: Explain how friction helps or hinders the intended job.
Use an observation or a clearly labelled model to support an idea.
vocabulary: A force that resists sliding, or attempted sliding, between touching surfaces.
The outside face of an object where contact happens.
A substance that can reduce friction in suitable contacts.
facts: Friction acts at a contact. Identify both surfaces and their relative sliding.
The actual surface pair and its condition matter. Smooth rubber and smooth glass can still grip; roughness alone does not predict every result.
Rubbing can transfer energy to thermal stores. A brief rub need not produce noticeable warmth.
model: For a box sliding right on a floor, friction on the box acts left along the contact. This is an explanatory model, not a force measurement.
examples: Helpful: pad–wheel friction helps a bike brake slow the wheel.
Unhelpful: rubbing between moving engine parts can cause unwanted heating and wear.
comparison: Compare surfaces using the same block, fixed ramp and release point, no push, and the same measuring start. Repeat a run. Record what actually happened; label supplied results as model data.
exit_intro: Two small checks to finish Lesson A. Point, say, sign, draw, type or use paper. An adult can scribe your words. You may pass; complete one route, once.

supported.label: Supported
questions: A box slides right on a floor. Which way does friction on the box act?
Bike brake pads rub on the wheel rim. Does this help slow the wheel?
answers: Left. Friction on this sliding box acts along the contact, against its slide to the right.
Yes. Pad–rim friction helps slow the wheel. The touching surfaces and the intended job make this a helpful example.

standard.label: Standard
questions: Friction acts between touching ____ and resists their sliding.
Friction at the brake pad helps the wheel ____.
answers: Surfaces. Accept a clear equivalent that identifies the two contacting surfaces.
Slow down or stop. The brake pad and rim resist sliding against one another.

stretch.label: Stretch
questions: Friction at a bike brake is helpful because ____.
Friction between moving engine parts can be unhelpful because ____.
answers: The pad and rim contact; friction resists their relative sliding and helps slow the wheel.
Unwanted rubbing can heat and wear moving parts. Judge friction against the intended job, not as an always-bad force.
